0461adc7-afe1-4d07-8245-8121bd245411.name: Bachelor of Business
0461adc7-afe1-4d07-8245-8121bd245411.description:
The Bachelor of Business at Holmes Institute is a three year degree covering management, strategy, marketing, economics and international business, with the option to add one of seven specialisations (Information Systems, Accounting, Marketing, Aviation Management, Management, Digital Business or Hospitality Management). The course runs across Holmes's Melbourne, Sydney, Brisbane and Gold Coast campuses with five intakes a year (March, May, July, September and November), so students who miss a start date rarely wait long. Teaching mixes case studies, simulations and assessments designed to mirror real workplace problems rather than pure lecture theory, and the final year includes a capstone Integrated Business Management Project.

Graduates typically move into roles such as business analyst, marketing coordinator, HR officer, operations supervisor or project coordinator, with longer term progression toward business development manager, HR manager, strategy consultant or general manager roles. As a smaller private higher education provider rather than a large public university, Holmes leans on small class sizes and direct lecturer access as its main point of difference, and the specialisation structure lets students bolt on a second area (for example Accounting or Digital Business) without switching degrees.
0461adc7-afe1-4d07-8245-8121bd245411.curriculum:
The Bachelor of Business comprises 12 core units, 2 specialisations (8 units) and 4 electives across 3 years.
Year 1 core: HC1001 Business Fundamentals; HC1041 Information Technology for Business; HC1021 Interpersonal and Electronic Communication; HC1031 Managing People and Organisations; HC1062 Decision Making and Problem Solving; HC1072 Economics and International Trade; HC1010 Accounting for Business; HC1082 Marketing.
Year 2 core: HC2001 Law in the Workplace; HC1052 Organisational Behaviour; HC2121 Comparative Business Ethics and Social Responsibility; plus specialisation units 1a, 2a, 1b, 2b, 1c.
Year 3: specialisation units 2c, 1d, 2d; electives; and HC3131 Integrated Business Management Project (capstone).
Specialisation choices: Information Systems, Accounting, Marketing, Aviation Management, Management, Digital Business, Hospitality Management. Electives may be chosen from other Holmes bachelor units where prerequisites are met, and elective and specialisation units are offered subject to demand.
0461adc7-afe1-4d07-8245-8121bd245411.admission_requirements: Successful completion of an Australian Year 12 (senior high school), a Certificate IV or equivalent; or successful completion of an approved Tertiary Preparation Program or a Foundation Year program offered by an accredited institution of higher education. No ATAR is separately quoted on the course page; full detail sits in Holmes's Admission Requirements Policy and Procedures document.
0461adc7-afe1-4d07-8245-8121bd245411.english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 with no band score lower than 5.5; or PTE Academic score of 46; or TOEFL iBT score of 60 to 78; or Cambridge English Advanced (CAE) score of 169; or successful completion of Year 12 at an Australian high school or an Australian Diploma or higher qualification; or successful completion of studies at a recognised Australian educational institution at an equivalent level with at least a 50 percent pass rate in a recent semester.

89a1762b-0b9b-498a-93f4-cbba34e19dbc.name: Bachelor of Fashion Business
89a1762b-0b9b-498a-93f4-cbba34e19dbc.description:
The Bachelor of Fashion Business is Holmes Institute's three year, fully online degree for students who want to work on the commercial side of fashion rather than design itself, covering marketing, merchandising, retail management, styling, e-commerce and global fashion strategy. It runs across four core themes (Marketing Engagement, Product Development, Business Skills and Fashion Contexts) with only March and July intakes, and the final year has students build their own fashion business plan and a portfolio aimed at employers.

Graduate roles are entry level (fashion marketing assistant, buying assistant, stylist assistant, e-commerce assistant, brand or marketing coordinator) with progression toward creative director, global fashion marketing manager or retail group general manager roles. Because the course is delivered fully online with no campus attendance, it suits students combining study with existing retail or fashion industry work, and international applicants must attend an interview and complete a skills assessment as part of admission, in addition to the standard document checks.
89a1762b-0b9b-498a-93f4-cbba34e19dbc.curriculum:
The Bachelor of Fashion Business comprises 22 core units and 2 electives across 3 years.
Year 1 (8 core units): HF1001 Visual Design Technologies; HF1002 Textiles and Materials; HF1004 Professional Communication and Ethics; HF1201 The Fashion Cycle; HF1003 Consumer Behaviour; HF1005 Product Development Strategies; HF1204 Principles of Fashion Management; HF1206 Fashion Finance and Accounting.
Year 2 (8 core units): HF2001 Research Methods and Market Intelligence; HF2005 Fashion History and Cultural Movements; HF2201 Brand Development; HF2202 Supply Chain Management and Analysis; HF2003 Fashion Tech; HF2013 Styling; HF2203 Buying and Financial Decision Making; HF2207 Fashion Marketing Strategies.
Year 3 (6 core units plus 2 electives): HF3001 Creative Business Project 1; HF3205 Visual Merchandising and Inventory Management; HF3207 E-Commerce and Digital Marketing; HF3208 Law and the Creative Industries; HF3002 Creative Business Project 2; HF3204 Modern Fashion Economies; electives chosen from HF3206 Content Creation and Collaboration, HFE2011 Copywriting and Digital Content, or a unit from the Bachelor of Business or Bachelor of Information Systems as approved by the Course Convener.
89a1762b-0b9b-498a-93f4-cbba34e19dbc.admission_requirements: Successful completion of Year 12 or equivalent; no ATAR required. Domestic applicants may need to provide a scanned Passport, Birth Certificate or Citizenship Certificate plus an academic certificate (or VTAC authorisation for Victorian students); students still completing Year 12 may apply for a Conditional Offer. International applicants must additionally attend an interview and complete a skills assessment with Holmes Institute. Full detail sits in the Admissions Requirements Policy and Procedures document.
89a1762b-0b9b-498a-93f4-cbba34e19dbc.english_requirements: Proof of English via one of Holmes's approved English test providers; the course page does not itself publish a minimum IELTS/PTE score (unlike Holmes's business and IT bachelor pages), and instead defers entirely to the Admissions Requirements Policy and Procedures document and, for international applicants, an interview and skills assessment.

283eb7d9-5887-44a7-beec-10e220c8e240.name: Bachelor of Information Systems
283eb7d9-5887-44a7-beec-10e220c8e240.description:
The Bachelor of Information Systems is Holmes Institute's three year IT and business degree, built around the Australian Computer Society's core body of knowledge, covering programming, database design, systems analysis, enterprise systems, business intelligence, human computer interaction, information security and a machine learning and artificial intelligence unit in the second year. It runs across Melbourne, Sydney and Gold Coast with five intakes a year (March, May, July, September and November).

Graduates are prepared for roles such as business analyst, systems analyst, IT consultant, data analyst, project coordinator or web/systems developer, with longer term progression toward IT manager, enterprise systems specialist or CIO. The degree sits alongside Holmes's Master of Information Systems as a direct pathway, and the elective structure lets students borrow units from Holmes's other bachelor degrees (Business, Fashion Business) where prerequisites are met.
283eb7d9-5887-44a7-beec-10e220c8e240.curriculum:
The Bachelor of Information Systems comprises 19 core units plus 5 electives across 3 years.
Year 1: HC1041 Information Technology for Business; HS1031 Introduction to Programming; HC1021 Interpersonal and Electronic Communication; HS1011 Data Communications and Networks; HC1001 Business Fundamentals; HC1062 Decision Making and Problem Solving; HS2011 Systems Analysis and Design; HS2021 Database Design and Use.
Year 2: HS2121 Professional Issues in IS, Ethics and Practice; HS2061 Information Systems Project Management; HS2041 Enterprise Systems; HS2031 Human Computer Interaction; HS1021 Web Design; HS3203 Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence; plus 2 electives.
Year 3: HS3021 Strategic Information Systems Management; HS3041 Business Intelligence and Knowledge Management; HS3011 Information Security; HC1031 Managing People and Organisations; HS3052 Capstone Project; plus 3 electives. Electives may be chosen from other Holmes bachelor units where prerequisites are met, subject to demand.
283eb7d9-5887-44a7-beec-10e220c8e240.admission_requirements: Successful completion of an Australian Year 12 (senior high school), a Certificate IV or equivalent; or successful completion of an approved Tertiary Preparation Program or a Foundation Year program offered by an accredited institution of higher education.
283eb7d9-5887-44a7-beec-10e220c8e240.english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 with no band score lower than 5.5; or PTE Academic score of 46; or TOEFL iBT score of 60 to 78; or Cambridge English Advanced (CAE) score of 169; or successful completion of Year 12 at an Australian high school or an Australian Diploma or higher qualification; or successful completion of studies at a recognised Australian educational institution at an equivalent level with at least a 50 percent pass rate in a recent semester.

6bfa11fe-01ad-4f27-8310-6ab45ce8597f.name: Bachelor of Professional Accounting
6bfa11fe-01ad-4f27-8310-6ab45ce8597f.description:
The Bachelor of Professional Accounting is Holmes Institute's three year accounting degree, designed to meet the academic requirements of CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand for professional accreditation. It covers financial and management accounting, auditing, taxation law, corporate finance and business law alongside core business units, running across Holmes's Melbourne, Sydney, Brisbane and Gold Coast campuses.

Graduates typically move into roles such as accounts officer, tax consultant, auditor, financial analyst or bookkeeper, with a direct pathway into Holmes's own Master of Professional Accounting for students who want to add a postgraduate qualification and meet the full CPA/CA membership pathway.
6bfa11fe-01ad-4f27-8310-6ab45ce8597f.curriculum: The Bachelor of Professional Accounting shares its business core with the Bachelor of Business (HC1001 Business Fundamentals; HC1041 Information Technology for Business; HC1021 Interpersonal and Electronic Communication; HC1031 Managing People and Organisations; HC1062 Decision Making and Problem Solving; HC1072 Economics and International Trade; HC1010 Accounting for Business; HC1082 Marketing; HC2001 Law in the Workplace; HC1052 Organisational Behaviour; HC2121 Comparative Business Ethics and Social Responsibility) and layers in an accounting major covering corporate accounting, management accounting, auditing, taxation law and finance, with a capstone Integrated Business Management Project in the final year. Holmes's public course page defers unit level sequencing for the accounting major to its downloadable course guide rather than listing every accounting unit by code on the page itself.
6bfa11fe-01ad-4f27-8310-6ab45ce8597f.admission_requirements: Successful completion of an Australian Year 12 (senior high school), a Certificate IV or equivalent; or successful completion of an approved Tertiary Preparation Program or a Foundation Year program offered by an accredited institution of higher education.
6bfa11fe-01ad-4f27-8310-6ab45ce8597f.english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 with no band score lower than 5.5; or PTE Academic score of 46; or TOEFL iBT score of 60 to 78; or Cambridge English Advanced (CAE) score of 169; or successful completion of Year 12 at an Australian high school or an Australian Diploma or higher qualification; or successful completion of studies at a recognised Australian educational institution at an equivalent level with at least a 50 percent pass rate in a recent semester.

7bb92d1e-446b-4ac2-a02e-47abd904fdb2.name: Graduate Diploma of Business
7bb92d1e-446b-4ac2-a02e-47abd904fdb2.description:
The Graduate Diploma of Business is Holmes Institute's one year, full time postgraduate qualification for students who want to upskill quickly in core business disciplines or who are building toward the MBA. It covers accounting, finance, economics and statistics for business decisions, and every unit credits directly into the MBA, so students who continue can move straight into the second year of that degree without repeating subjects.

Graduates typically move into roles such as business analyst, marketing coordinator, HR officer, project supervisor or operations coordinator, with the course marketed explicitly as a stepping stone into senior business leadership or a direct MBA pathway rather than a terminal qualification.
7bb92d1e-446b-4ac2-a02e-47abd904fdb2.curriculum:
The Graduate Diploma in Business comprises 4 core units and 4 elective units.
Core: HI5001 Accounting for Business Decisions; HI5002 Finance for Business; HI5003 Economics for Business; HI6007 Statistics for Business Decisions.
Electives are chosen from other postgraduate courses offered by Holmes Institute, subject to demand and availability in a given study period.
7bb92d1e-446b-4ac2-a02e-47abd904fdb2.admission_requirements: An Australian Bachelor degree or equivalent; or an Australian Graduate Certificate; or an Advanced Diploma/Associate Degree (or overseas equivalent) plus a minimum of five years' demonstrable relevant industry experience.
7bb92d1e-446b-4ac2-a02e-47abd904fdb2.english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 with no band score lower than 5.5; or PTE Academic score of 46; or TOEFL iBT score of 60 to 78; or Cambridge English Advanced (CAE) score of 169; or successful completion of Year 12 at an Australian high school or an Australian Diploma or higher qualification; or successful completion of studies at a recognised Australian educational institution at an equivalent level with at least a 50 percent pass rate in a recent semester.

1dafa365-8c9d-4850-b17c-378723613ebc.name: Graduate Diploma of Early Childhood
1dafa365-8c9d-4850-b17c-378723613ebc.description:
The Graduate Diploma of Early Childhood is Holmes Institute's one year postgraduate qualification for career changers moving into early childhood education, approved by the Australian Children's Education and Care Quality Authority (ACECQA) as equivalent to an approved educator qualification under the National Quality Framework. It combines coursework in child development, pedagogy and inclusive practice with a supervised professional placement, and every unit credits into the second year of the Master of Teaching (Early Childhood) for students who continue toward full teacher registration.

Graduates typically move into roles such as childcare educator, early childhood assistant or early learning support officer, with progression toward the Master of Teaching (Early Childhood) as the main long term pathway.
1dafa365-8c9d-4850-b17c-378723613ebc.curriculum:
The Graduate Diploma of Early Childhood comprises 7 core units plus 1 elective.
Core: HT5001 Foundations of Education Development; HT5002 Perspectives on Teaching, Learning and Development; HT5003 Children's Play, Creativity and the Arts; HT5004 Professional Placement 1; HT5005 Working as an Early Childhood Professional; HT5006 Children's Language and Literacy; HT5007 Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM).
Elective: Graduate Diploma students must complete HT5008 for this elective to have their qualification recognised by ACECQA.
1dafa365-8c9d-4850-b17c-378723613ebc.admission_requirements: An Australian Bachelor degree or equivalent; or an Australian Graduate Diploma; or an Australian Graduate Certificate or equivalent plus a minimum of two years' demonstrable relevant industry experience; or an Advanced Diploma/Associate Degree or equivalent plus a minimum of five years' demonstrable relevant industry experience.
1dafa365-8c9d-4850-b17c-378723613ebc.english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 with no band score lower than 6.0; or PTE Academic score of 46; or TOEFL iBT score of 60 to 78; or Cambridge English Advanced (CAE) score of 169; or successful completion of Year 12 at an Australian high school or an Australian Diploma or higher qualification; or successful completion of studies at a recognised Australian educational institution at an equivalent level with at least a 50 percent pass rate in a recent semester.

3a6b2636-fd44-446e-a2e7-fd7482b6bd35.name: Master of Business Administration
3a6b2636-fd44-446e-a2e7-fd7482b6bd35.description:
The Holmes Institute MBA is a 1.5 year, full time postgraduate degree across Melbourne, Sydney, Brisbane and Gold Coast, built around 8 core units in accounting, economics, finance, marketing, statistics, management, strategy and business research, plus 4 electives that can be taken as a single specialisation (Information Systems, Accounting, or International Business and Enterprise) or spread across specialisations for a generic MBA. Students may also exit early with a Graduate Certificate in Business after 1 trimester (the first 4 core units) or a Graduate Diploma in Business after 2 trimesters (8 units), both of which credit fully into a later return to the MBA.

As a smaller private provider rather than a Group of Eight university, the degree does not carry sandstone brand weight, and most graduates use it to move into management roles in small to mid sized organisations or to support a skilled migration pathway rather than to break into top tier consulting. It suits applicants who already have a bachelor's degree or several years of relevant industry experience and want a generalist management toolkit without relocating overseas or leaving the workforce for two years.
3a6b2636-fd44-446e-a2e7-fd7482b6bd35.curriculum:
The Holmes Institute MBA is typically completed in 1.5 years full time and comprises 8 core units and 4 electives.
Core units: HI5001 Accounting for Business Decisions (or HM5001 Accounting for Managers); HI5003 Economics for Business (or HM5003 Economics for Managers); HI5002 Finance for Business (or HM5002 Finance for Managers); HI5004 Marketing Management; HI6007 Statistics for Business Decisions (or HM6007 Statistics for Managers); HI6005 Management of Organisations in a Global Environment; HI6006 Competitive Strategy; HI6008 Business Research.
Electives: 4 units chosen from the same specialisation (Information Systems, Accounting, or International Business and Enterprise) for an MBA with one specialisation, or across specialisations for a generic MBA. Exit points: Graduate Certificate in Business after 1 trimester (the first 4 core units); Graduate Diploma in Business after 2 trimesters (8 units).
3a6b2636-fd44-446e-a2e7-fd7482b6bd35.admission_requirements: An Australian Bachelor degree or equivalent; or an Australian Graduate Diploma; or an Australian Graduate Certificate or equivalent plus a minimum of two years' demonstrable relevant industry experience; or an Advanced Diploma/Associate Degree or equivalent plus a minimum of five years' demonstrable relevant industry experience.
3a6b2636-fd44-446e-a2e7-fd7482b6bd35.english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 with no band score lower than 5.5; or PTE Academic score of 46; or TOEFL iBT score of 60 to 78; or Cambridge English Advanced (CAE) score of 169; or successful completion of Year 12 at an Australian high school or an Australian Diploma or higher qualification; or successful completion of studies at a recognised Australian educational institution at an equivalent level with at least a 50 percent pass rate in a recent semester.

70b93527-d01f-4ff0-87be-833df9d618c3.name: Master of Business Administration (Professional)
70b93527-d01f-4ff0-87be-833df9d618c3.description:
The MBA (Professional) is Holmes Institute's 2 year, full time extended MBA for students who want to go deeper than the standard 1.5 year MBA, doubling the elective load to 8 units so students can complete one or two specialisations (Accounting, International Business and Enterprise, Healthcare Management, Information Systems or Project Management) alongside the same 8 core units as the standard MBA.

The course is marketed at aspiring executives, entrepreneurs and consultants who want both practical business skills and the depth to lead innovation and change, and it shares the same accounting, economics, finance, marketing, statistics, management, strategy and research core as Holmes's standard MBA, differing mainly in the size and structure of its elective/specialisation block.
70b93527-d01f-4ff0-87be-833df9d618c3.curriculum:
The MBA (Professional) comprises 8 core units and 8 elective units.
Core units: HI5001 Accounting for Business Decisions (or HM5001 Accounting for Managers); HI5003 Economics for Business (or HM5003 Economics for Managers); HI5002 Finance for Business (or HM5002 Finance for Managers); HI5004 Marketing Management; HI6007 Statistics for Business Decisions (or HM6007 Statistics for Managers); HI6005 Management of Organisations in a Global Environment; HI6006 Competitive Strategy; HI6008 Business Research.
Electives: 8 units, structured as a single specialisation (8 units) or two specialisations (4 units each) chosen from Accounting, International Business and Enterprise, Healthcare Management, Information Systems or Project Management, or across specialisations for a generic MBA (Professional).
70b93527-d01f-4ff0-87be-833df9d618c3.admission_requirements: An Australian Bachelor degree or equivalent; or an Australian Graduate Diploma; or an Australian Graduate Certificate or equivalent plus a minimum of two years' demonstrable relevant industry experience; or an Advanced Diploma/Associate Degree or equivalent plus a minimum of five years' demonstrable relevant industry experience.
70b93527-d01f-4ff0-87be-833df9d618c3.english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 with no band score lower than 6.0; or PTE Academic score of 46; or TOEFL iBT score of 60 to 78; or Cambridge English Advanced (CAE) score of 169; or successful completion of Year 12 at an Australian high school or an Australian Diploma or higher qualification; or successful completion of studies at a recognised Australian educational institution at an equivalent level with at least a 50 percent pass rate in a recent semester.

5aea75de-11db-48d7-953f-6412d1e64791.name: Master of Cyber Security
5aea75de-11db-48d7-953f-6412d1e64791.description:
The Master of Cyber Security is Holmes Institute's 2 year, full time, TEQSA accredited postgraduate degree at its Melbourne campus, combining technical skills (network security, cyber forensics, cloud security) with the management and governance side of the field so graduates can both design secure systems and lead security strategy inside an organisation. Holmes runs two entry paths through the same course, a 12 unit non cognate structure for applicants with no prior computing study and a 10 core plus 2 elective cognate structure for applicants who have already studied computing.

Graduates typically move into roles such as cybersecurity analyst, IT security specialist, risk and compliance analyst, cyber forensics investigator or incident response manager, with progression toward CISO, cybersecurity policy advisor or senior security architect roles.
5aea75de-11db-48d7-953f-6412d1e64791.curriculum:
Non cognate structure (no prior computing study), 12 core units: Semester 1: HS7000 Information Systems in Business; HS7001 Data and Information Management; HS7002 IS Governance, Security and Ethics. Semester 2: HS7020 Cyber Criminology; HS7021 Programming Fundamentals; HS7022 Project Management. Semester 3: HS7030 Networks and Data Communications; HS7031 Information Security Management; HS7032 Cyber Forensics. Semester 4: HS7040 Network Security; HS7041 Business Intelligence; HS7042 Cyber Security Project.
Cognate structure (previous study in computing), 10 core units plus 2 electives: Semester 1: HS7021 Programming Fundamentals; HS7020 Cyber Criminology; HS7002 IS Governance, Security and Ethics. Semester 2: HS7022 Project Management; HS7041 Business Intelligence; 1 elective. Semester 3: HS7030 Networks and Data Communications; HS7031 Information Security Management; HS7032 Cyber Forensics. Semester 4: HS7040 Network Security; 1 elective; HS7042 Cyber Security Project.
Electives: HS7050 Cloud Security; HS7051 Internet of Things Security; HS7043 Artificial Intelligence.
5aea75de-11db-48d7-953f-6412d1e64791.admission_requirements: An Australian Bachelor degree or equivalent; or an Australian Graduate Diploma; or an Australian Graduate Certificate or equivalent plus a minimum of two years' demonstrable relevant industry experience; or an Advanced Diploma/Associate Degree or equivalent plus a minimum of five years' demonstrable relevant industry experience.
5aea75de-11db-48d7-953f-6412d1e64791.english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 with no band score lower than 6.0; or PTE Academic score of 56; or TOEFL iBT score of 79 to 93; or Cambridge English Advanced (CAE) score of 176; or successful completion of an Australian bachelor degree.

c66da96d-bc09-44ff-9d23-7287a90f89d6.name: Master of Information Systems
c66da96d-bc09-44ff-9d23-7287a90f89d6.description:
The Master of Information Systems is Holmes Institute's 2 year, full time postgraduate degree for both IT and non IT graduates who want to move into IT strategy, enterprise systems, business analytics or data driven decision making, with an optional specialisation in Cybersecurity or Business Analytics. Students may exit early with a Graduate Certificate in Information Systems after 1 trimester (4 units) or a Graduate Diploma of Information Systems after 2 trimesters (8 units), both of which credit fully into a later return to the Master's.

Graduates typically move into roles such as business analyst, systems analyst, IT consultant, project manager, data analyst or enterprise systems specialist, with progression toward IT director, CIO, head of digital transformation or senior technology consultant roles.
c66da96d-bc09-44ff-9d23-7287a90f89d6.curriculum:
The Master of Information Systems comprises 12 core units, 1 elective and 3 specialisation units.
Year 1: HM6032 Leveraging IS for Business Advantage; HI5033 Database Design; HI5030 Systems Analysis and Design; HI5031 Professional Issues in IS, Ethics and Practice; HI5029 IS Project Management; HI6035 IS Governance and Risk; HI6037 Business Analytics Fundamentals; 1 elective.
Year 2: 3 specialisation units (chosen from Cybersecurity: Information Security Systems, Computer Forensics and Analysis, Computer Network Security; or Business Analytics: Data Visualisation, Predictive Analytics, AI/Machine Learning); HI6034 Enterprise Information Systems; HI6036 IS Strategy and Innovation; HM6007 Statistics for Business; HI6008 Business Research Methods; HI6050 Contemporary Workplace Project.
Exit points: Graduate Certificate in Information Systems after 1 trimester (4 units); Graduate Diploma of Information Systems after 2 trimesters (8 units).
c66da96d-bc09-44ff-9d23-7287a90f89d6.admission_requirements: An Australian Bachelor degree or equivalent; or an Australian Graduate Diploma; or an Australian Graduate Certificate or equivalent plus a minimum of two years' demonstrable relevant industry experience; or an Advanced Diploma/Associate Degree or equivalent plus a minimum of five years' demonstrable relevant industry experience.
c66da96d-bc09-44ff-9d23-7287a90f89d6.english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 with no band score lower than 6.0; or PTE Academic score of 56; or TOEFL iBT score of 79 to 93; or Cambridge English Advanced (CAE) score of 176; or successful completion of an Australian bachelor degree.

38cd532c-0bd2-4bbc-a937-1f9cb386c701.name: Master of Professional Accounting
38cd532c-0bd2-4bbc-a937-1f9cb386c701.description:
The Master of Professional Accounting is Holmes Institute's postgraduate accounting degree, aimed at graduates from a non accounting background who want to meet the academic requirements for CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand membership. It covers financial accounting, management accounting, auditing, taxation law, corporate law and finance at postgraduate depth, and runs across Holmes's Melbourne, Sydney, Brisbane and Gold Coast campuses.

Graduates typically move into roles such as accountant, auditor, tax consultant or financial analyst, with the degree positioned as the standard postgraduate accounting conversion pathway for international students holding a non accounting bachelor's degree.
38cd532c-0bd2-4bbc-a937-1f9cb386c701.curriculum: Holmes Institute's public course page for the Master of Professional Accounting states entry requirements and CRICOS details but defers the semester by semester unit list to its downloadable course guide rather than publishing individual unit codes on the page itself; the degree covers financial accounting, management accounting, auditing, taxation law, corporate law and corporate finance at postgraduate level, consistent with CPA Australia and CA ANZ accreditation requirements.
38cd532c-0bd2-4bbc-a937-1f9cb386c701.admission_requirements: An Australian Bachelor degree or equivalent; or an Australian Graduate Diploma; or an Australian Graduate Certificate or equivalent plus a minimum of two years' demonstrable relevant industry experience; or an Advanced Diploma/Associate Degree or equivalent plus a minimum of five years' demonstrable relevant industry experience.
38cd532c-0bd2-4bbc-a937-1f9cb386c701.english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 with no band score lower than 6.0; or PTE Academic score of 56; or TOEFL iBT score of 79 to 93; or Cambridge English Advanced (CAE) score of 176; or successful completion of an Australian bachelor degree.

b0bd9eed-0a00-482f-8452-1b9b858a1d9b.name: Master of Teaching (Early Childhood)
b0bd9eed-0a00-482f-8452-1b9b858a1d9b.description:
The Master of Teaching (Early Childhood) is Holmes Institute's 2 year, full time initial teacher education degree, approved by ACECQA and designed to lead to full early childhood teacher registration. It combines child development theory, curriculum design and inclusive teaching practice with two supervised professional placements, and the first year of units is identical to Holmes's Graduate Diploma of Early Childhood, so Graduate Diploma graduates can move directly into the second year without repeating subjects.

Because it leads to a registrable teaching qualification, admission carries a non academic bar the rest of Holmes's postgraduate courses do not: applicants must complete a teaching suitability test or interview (Holmes uses the Casper situational judgement test administered by Acuity Insights) to confirm they are ready to participate in professional placements. Graduates typically move into roles such as early childhood teacher or kindergarten teacher, with progression toward centre director, early years consultant or policy advisor roles.
b0bd9eed-0a00-482f-8452-1b9b858a1d9b.curriculum:
The Master of Teaching (Early Childhood) comprises 15 core units and 1 elective across 2 years.
Year 1 (shared with the Graduate Diploma of Early Childhood): HT5001 Foundations of Education Development; HT5002 Perspectives on Teaching, Learning and Development; HT5003 Children's Play, Creativity and the Arts; HT5004 Professional Placement 1; HT5005 Working as an Early Childhood Professional; HT5006 Children's Language and Literacy; HT5007 Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM); 1 elective.
Year 2: HT5008 Professional Placement 2; HT6010 Children, Families and Communities; HT6011 Assessing Child Learning and Development; HT6012 Diversity and Inclusion in Early Childhood Practice; HT6013 Understanding and Supporting Children with Additional Needs; HT6014 Leading and Managing in Early Childhood Settings; HT6015 Research for Early Childhood Professionals; HT6016 Health, Nutrition, Ethics, Safety and Protection.
Electives: HT6017 Education Governance and Management; HT6018 Contemporary Issues in Early Childhood Education.
b0bd9eed-0a00-482f-8452-1b9b858a1d9b.admission_requirements: An Australian Bachelor degree or equivalent; or an Australian Graduate Diploma; or an Australian Graduate Certificate or equivalent plus a minimum of two years' demonstrable relevant industry experience; or an Advanced Diploma/Associate Degree or equivalent plus a minimum of five years' demonstrable relevant industry experience. Applicants must also complete a teaching suitability test or interview (the Casper situational judgement test, administered online by Acuity Insights at scheduled sitting times) to confirm readiness for professional experience placements.
b0bd9eed-0a00-482f-8452-1b9b858a1d9b.english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.0 with no band score lower than 6.5; or PTE Academic score of 66; or TOEFL iBT score of 94 to 101; or Cambridge English Advanced (CAE) score of 185; or successful completion of an Australian bachelor degree or higher.

1ef19919-a230-434c-be8d-03a19bcfcd69.name: Undergraduate Certificate in Fashion Business
1ef19919-a230-434c-be8d-03a19bcfcd69.description:
The Undergraduate Certificate in Fashion Business is Holmes Institute's one semester (14 week), fully online introduction to the fashion industry's commercial side, aimed at people who want a taste of fashion business before committing to the full three year Bachelor of Fashion Business, or a fast, standalone credential for a career change. It comprises 2 core units plus 2 electives chosen from the Bachelor of Fashion Business's own first year units, and it credits with advanced standing directly into that Bachelor if a student continues.

The course has only a March intake and no campus attendance requirement. It is not marketed as a job qualification on its own so much as a low-commitment entry point and a genuine, currently accredited pathway product sitting alongside Holmes's fashion bachelor degree.
1ef19919-a230-434c-be8d-03a19bcfcd69.curriculum:
The Undergraduate Certificate in Fashion Business comprises 2 core units and 2 elective units, chosen from first year Bachelor of Fashion Business units.
Core: HF1201 The Fashion Cycle; HF1001 Visual Design Technologies.
Electives (choose 2): HF1004 Professional Communication and Ethics; HF1002 Textiles and Materials; HF1206 Fashion Finance and Accounting.
Electives may also be chosen from other undergraduate courses offered by Holmes Institute, subject to demand.
1ef19919-a230-434c-be8d-03a19bcfcd69.admission_requirements: Successful completion of Year 12 or equivalent; no ATAR required.
1ef19919-a230-434c-be8d-03a19bcfcd69.english_requirements: Proof of English via one of Holmes's approved English test providers; the course page does not itself publish a minimum IELTS/PTE score, deferring to the Admissions Requirements Policy and Procedures document.

72a8a34e-ace8-4611-8122-557af9238501.name: Associate Degree of Aviation
72a8a34e-ace8-4611-8122-557af9238501.description:
The Associate Degree of Aviation is a real, currently TEQSA accredited (renewal date 17/03/2030) and CRICOS registered qualification of Holmes Institute (CRICOS 112847K, delivered from Melbourne's Moorabbin campus per its most recent live course page). It is not currently listed on holmes.edu.au's own sitemap, its aviation faculty page, or the institution's official 2026 Aviation Course Guide, which now markets only three aviation programs: Bachelor of Aviation (Flight) majoring in Piloting, Bachelor of Aviation (Flight) majoring in Drone Operations, and Bachelor of Aviation (Management). A dedicated course page for this Associate Degree existed on the aviation.holmes.edu.au subdomain as recently as October 2023 (confirmed via the Wayback Machine, matching CRICOS code 112847K) but now returns a 404.

Given the qualification's real, current government accreditation, this row is not being archived, but Holmes does not currently publish a course overview, learning outcomes or curriculum for it anywhere.
72a8a34e-ace8-4611-8122-557af9238501.admission_requirements: Not published on any current Holmes Institute page; the 2023 archived course page (no longer live) stated Year 12 completion with no ATAR required, consistent with Holmes's general Diploma/Associate Degree tier.
72a8a34e-ace8-4611-8122-557af9238501.english_requirements: Not published on any current Holmes Institute page.
72a8a34e-ace8-4611-8122-557af9238501.source_url: https://cricos.education.gov.au/ (CRICOS 112847K, Holmes Institute Pty Ltd, Associate Degree, active registration)

42468405-fd0e-44fc-a8d4-082b63b94649.name: Diploma of Business Management
42468405-fd0e-44fc-a8d4-082b63b94649.description:
The Diploma of Business Management is Holmes Institute's embedded exit award from the Bachelor of Business: a third party education agent listing (IDP) directly quotes Holmes as stating that 'students can exit the Bachelor of Business after successfully completing the first year units and be awarded the Diploma of Business Management qualification (DBM)'. It is a real, currently CRICOS registered qualification (074264G, Course Sector: Higher Education) but does not have its own dedicated marketing page on the current holmes.edu.au site; the most recent Holmes owned page found for it is a 2012 Wayback Machine snapshot describing it as covering management, marketing, accounting, IT, economics and HR with IELTS 6.0 as the international English bar at the time.

Because it is the Bachelor of Business's own first year packaged as a standalone credit, its content maps directly onto that degree's confirmed current Year 1 units rather than a separately designed curriculum.
42468405-fd0e-44fc-a8d4-082b63b94649.curriculum: As the embedded first year exit award from the Bachelor of Business, this Diploma's units are the Bachelor's own confirmed Year 1 core: HC1001 Business Fundamentals; HC1041 Information Technology for Business; HC1021 Interpersonal and Electronic Communication; HC1031 Managing People and Organisations; HC1062 Decision Making and Problem Solving; HC1072 Economics and International Trade; HC1010 Accounting for Business; HC1082 Marketing.
42468405-fd0e-44fc-a8d4-082b63b94649.admission_requirements: Successful completion of an Australian Year 12 (senior high school), a Certificate IV or equivalent; or successful completion of an approved Tertiary Preparation Program or a Foundation Year program offered by an accredited institution of higher education (same Diploma/Bachelor tier as the Bachelor of Business it exits from).
42468405-fd0e-44fc-a8d4-082b63b94649.english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 with no band score lower than 5.5 (Holmes's general Diploma and Bachelor tier); a 2012 archived Holmes page for this specific course also quoted IELTS 6.0 as the international requirement at that time.
42468405-fd0e-44fc-a8d4-082b63b94649.source_url: https://www.idp.com/universities-and-colleges/holmes-institute/bachelor-of-business-058264g/PRG-AU-00375547/ (embedded exit award confirmation); https://cricos.education.gov.au/ (CRICOS 074264G, active registration)

27060f58-9373-4ed2-b1bc-196e4cbf3e2f.name: Graduate Certificate in Business
27060f58-9373-4ed2-b1bc-196e4cbf3e2f.description:
The Graduate Certificate in Business is Holmes Institute's embedded one trimester exit award from the MBA: a third party education agent listing (IDP) directly quotes Holmes as stating that 'students may elect to exit the MBA after one trimester having qualified for the Graduate Certificate in Business (GCB) award which consists of 4 units'. It is a real, currently CRICOS registered qualification (102190G) named explicitly, alongside the Graduate Diploma in Business and MBA, in Holmes's own current Admission Requirements Policy and Procedures document, but it has no dedicated marketing page on holmes.edu.au (its own 2019 page, since removed, is preserved in the Wayback Machine).

Because the Graduate Certificate is the same 4 core units that make up the whole Graduate Diploma in Business (which itself has a live current course page), its curriculum maps directly onto that confirmed real unit list.
27060f58-9373-4ed2-b1bc-196e4cbf3e2f.curriculum: As the embedded first trimester exit award from the MBA (and identical to the Graduate Diploma in Business's own 4 core units), this Graduate Certificate comprises: HI5001 Accounting for Business Decisions; HI5002 Finance for Business; HI5003 Economics for Business; HI6007 Statistics for Business Decisions.
27060f58-9373-4ed2-b1bc-196e4cbf3e2f.admission_requirements: An Australian Bachelor degree or equivalent; or a Diploma or equivalent plus a minimum of five years' demonstrable relevant industry experience (Holmes's Graduate Certificate tier, per its current Admission Requirements Policy and Procedures document).
27060f58-9373-4ed2-b1bc-196e4cbf3e2f.english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 with no band score lower than 5.5; or PTE Academic score of 46; or TOEFL iBT score of 60 to 78; or Cambridge English Advanced (CAE) score of 169 (the same tier as the Graduate Diploma in Business and MBA, per Holmes's current Admission Requirements Policy and Procedures document).
27060f58-9373-4ed2-b1bc-196e4cbf3e2f.source_url: https://www.idp.com/universities-and-colleges/holmes-institute/master-of-business-administration/PRG-AU-00180029/ (embedded exit award confirmation); Holmes Institute Admission Requirements Policy and Procedures v2.9 (named English requirement tier); https://cricos.education.gov.au/ (CRICOS 102190G, active registration)

8ed7845b-ae9c-4fe7-b923-0cc32dfbcbfb.name: Graduate Certificate in Information Systems
8ed7845b-ae9c-4fe7-b923-0cc32dfbcbfb.description:
The Graduate Certificate in Information Systems is Holmes Institute's embedded one trimester exit award from the Master of Information Systems: a third party education agent listing (IDP) directly quotes Holmes as stating that this award 'consists of 4 units' after one trimester, with a Graduate Diploma of Information Systems available after two trimesters (8 units). It is a real, currently CRICOS registered qualification (102298F) but has no dedicated marketing page on the current holmes.edu.au site, no historical page in the Wayback Machine, and is not individually named in Holmes's current Admission Requirements Policy document's English requirement list (unlike the Business faculty's equivalent Graduate Certificate).

Because this Graduate Certificate is confirmed as the first 4 units of the Master of Information Systems' own Year 1 core (which has a live, current course page), its likely curriculum maps onto that confirmed unit list, though the exact 4-of-8 split is not independently published.
8ed7845b-ae9c-4fe7-b923-0cc32dfbcbfb.curriculum: As the embedded first trimester exit award from the Master of Information Systems, this Graduate Certificate most likely comprises the first 4 of that Master's confirmed Year 1 core units: HM6032 Leveraging IS for Business Advantage; HI5033 Database Design; HI5030 Systems Analysis and Design; HI5031 Professional Issues in IS, Ethics and Practice. Holmes does not publish which 4 of the Master's 8 Year 1 units specifically make up this award, so this ordering is inferred from the Master's own published unit sequence, not independently confirmed.
8ed7845b-ae9c-4fe7-b923-0cc32dfbcbfb.admission_requirements: An Australian Bachelor degree or equivalent; or a Diploma or equivalent plus a minimum of five years' demonstrable relevant industry experience (Holmes's general Graduate Certificate tier, per its current Admission Requirements Policy and Procedures document).
8ed7845b-ae9c-4fe7-b923-0cc32dfbcbfb.english_requirements: Not individually named in Holmes's current Admission Requirements Policy document; the Master of Information Systems it exits from requires IELTS overall 6.5 with no band score lower than 6.0.
8ed7845b-ae9c-4fe7-b923-0cc32dfbcbfb.source_url: https://www.idp.com/universities-and-colleges/holmes-institute/master-of-information-systems/PRG-AU-00395882/ (embedded exit award confirmation); https://cricos.education.gov.au/ (CRICOS 102298F, active registration)

b262f20a-de2f-4c37-b405-6f4ffae1eff3.name: Graduate Diploma of Information Systems
b262f20a-de2f-4c37-b405-6f4ffae1eff3.description:
The Graduate Diploma of Information Systems is Holmes Institute's embedded two trimester exit award from the Master of Information Systems: a third party education agent listing (IDP) directly quotes Holmes as stating that this award 'consists of 8 units' after two trimesters, sitting between the 4 unit Graduate Certificate of Information Systems and the full 16 unit Master's degree. It is a real, currently CRICOS registered qualification (102297G, Course Sector: Higher Education, 52 week duration, $25,000 tuition) but has no dedicated marketing page on the current holmes.edu.au site and no historical page in the Wayback Machine.

Because this Graduate Diploma is confirmed as the whole of the Master of Information Systems' Year 1 (8 units), its curriculum maps directly onto that confirmed real unit list.
b262f20a-de2f-4c37-b405-6f4ffae1eff3.curriculum: As the embedded two trimester exit award from the Master of Information Systems (its full Year 1), this Graduate Diploma comprises: HM6032 Leveraging IS for Business Advantage; HI5033 Database Design; HI5030 Systems Analysis and Design; HI5031 Professional Issues in IS, Ethics and Practice; HI5029 IS Project Management; HI6035 IS Governance and Risk; HI6037 Business Analytics Fundamentals; plus 1 elective.
b262f20a-de2f-4c37-b405-6f4ffae1eff3.admission_requirements: An Australian Bachelor degree or equivalent; or an Australian Graduate Certificate; or an Advanced Diploma/Associate Degree (or overseas equivalent) plus a minimum of five years' demonstrable relevant industry experience (Holmes's Graduate Diploma tier, per its current Admission Requirements Policy and Procedures document).
b262f20a-de2f-4c37-b405-6f4ffae1eff3.english_requirements: Not individually named in Holmes's current Admission Requirements Policy document; the Master of Information Systems it exits from requires IELTS overall 6.5 with no band score lower than 6.0.
b262f20a-de2f-4c37-b405-6f4ffae1eff3.source_url: https://www.idp.com/universities-and-colleges/holmes-institute/master-of-information-systems/PRG-AU-00395882/ (embedded exit award confirmation); https://cricos.education.gov.au/ (CRICOS 102297G, active registration)

64b8792a-0ac4-41eb-9abc-f038eca3f8cb.name: Bachelor of Aviation (Management)
64b8792a-0ac4-41eb-9abc-f038eca3f8cb.description:
The Bachelor of Aviation (Management) is Holmes Institute's three year business side aviation degree, covering aviation law, airport and ground operations, airline operations, safety systems and human factors in aviation alongside business subjects in finance, marketing and organisational leadership. It runs at Melbourne's Moorabbin campus in partnership with Tristar Aviation, with March and July intakes, and sits alongside Holmes's flying majors (Piloting and Drone Operations) as the non-flying, operations and business focused aviation pathway.

Graduates typically move into roles such as airport operations manager, airline operations coordinator, aviation safety and compliance officer, ground operations manager or aviation business development officer, with progression toward airport general manager, airline operations director or head of airline strategy roles.
64b8792a-0ac4-41eb-9abc-f038eca3f8cb.curriculum:
The Bachelor of Aviation (Management) is studied over 3 years.
Year 1: Business Fundamentals; Aviation Professional and Study Foundations; Meteorology; Aviation Management (Semester 1); Aviation Law; Aerodynamics; Managing People and Organisations; 1 elective (Semester 2).
Year 2: Human Resource Management; International Aviation Systems; Human Factors in Aviation (Semester 1); Airspace Management Systems; Commercial Aviation Operations; 3 electives (Semester 2).
Year 3: Contemporary Issues in Aviation; Airport and Ground Operations; 2 electives (Semester 1); Aviation Safety Management; Aviation Research Project; 2 electives (Semester 2).
64b8792a-0ac4-41eb-9abc-f038eca3f8cb.admission_requirements: Successful completion of an Australian Year 12 (senior high school), a Certificate IV or equivalent; or successful completion of an approved Tertiary Preparation Program or a Foundation Year program offered by an accredited institution of higher education. No ATAR required. Assumed knowledge: Year 12 Mathematical Methods or equivalent.
64b8792a-0ac4-41eb-9abc-f038eca3f8cb.english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 with no band score lower than 5.5; or successful completion of Year 12 at an Australian high school or an Australian Diploma or higher qualification; or successful completion of studies at a recognised Australian educational institution at an equivalent level with at least a 50 percent pass rate in a recent semester.
